hits.draft_en:
Pieter asked his AI agent to check his nutrition data. Answer: about 200mg of magnesium a day against roughly 420mg recommended. 121k views.

The interesting part isn't the magnesium. It's that his food log already lives somewhere his agent can read it, so the question took one message.

hits.draft_en:
Alex Finn has tried most personal AI agents and says Claude Duet is the best so far: smartest (Opus 5.5), most proactive, friendliest. 85k views, 457 bookmarks.

hits.draft_en:
Pieter flagged that Product Hunt's 'Login with X' now asks for a lot of permissions and wondered if it's safer to skip it. 25k views, 149 replies.

Good habit for any 'Login with' button: read the permission screen before you click allow. If a launch site wants more than your name and avatar, ask why.

And if you build one, request the smallest scope that works. People notice.

outsiders.name: Google AI
outsiders.text:
Introducing Genie 4 from @GoogleDeepMind, our most realistic and interactive world model yet 🌍

Now you can use natural language to dynamically steer the world and its soundscape in real-time, whether you're changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing new elements to the environment.

So, how does the model do that?

Behind the scenes, Gemini acts as the "brain" of the simulation. It translates your requests into actions, plans out complex events, watches the scene unfold to keep track of what's happening, and adjusts as you change the story. Genie 4 also introduces ambient audio and real-time interactive human dialogue that adapts on the fly.

virals.angle: Give away the app, charge for the work
virals.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg's line got 167k views and 1.1k bookmarks: give away the CRM, the dashboard and the app, and charge for the agent that does the work.

Marc Lou called it 'the end of UI for SaaS' the next morning (139k). Amjad Masad: 'Software ate the world, now it's learning to run it.'

If you sell software, write down the one outcome customers pay for. That outcome, done by an agent, is what you'll be pricing next year.

virals.angle: One box, one agent, all your data
virals.draft_en:
Pieter Levels runs everything from VPS servers: Termius for SSH, Claude Code on the box, and his businesses, calories and sleep data all pulled in. The same setup told him he was short on magnesium (121k views).

Theo shared a similar setup: he controls his machines from his phone over the internet, not through computer use.

The pattern isn't a new app. It's putting your data where one agent can read it.

virals.angle: Agent that suggests vs agent you steer
virals.draft_en:
Two takes on Claude Duet in one day.

Alex Finn: the most intelligent, proactive and friendly personal agent he's tried (85k views).
Riley Brown: churned, back on Claude Code Projects, where he picks the model and can run sessions on his own computer (67k).

Both are right for different people. Do you want ideas handed to you, or control? Answer that before you pick a tool.

Hassan's Bygga walks you through IKEA assembly with interactive 3D and voice. Free, open source, 199k views and 2.4k bookmarks in a day.

Meanwhile, Genie 4 (2.95M on DeepMind's post) shows where interactive 3D is heading.

The saved posts this week weren't benchmarks. They were tools that make an annoying real-world task easier. Find one and build the guide you wish existed.

virals.angle: AI as a research partner, with receipts
virals.draft_en:
Greg Brockman announced three scientific results with AI help, in math, complexity theory and physics (3.08M views). Anthropic said it's in research partnerships with six drug developers and started its own discovery work (2.49M).

These are company claims, so read the papers before you repeat the headline.

But the practical lesson for the rest of us: use models to extend real data and prior work, then check the result, like Ethan Mollick's GPT-6 Pro crime-data rerun.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 27 ~11:15 CT (after Tuesday's digest) through Oct 28 ~11:15 CT. The most useful thread for builders was pricing: Greg Isenberg's 'give away the app, charge for the agent that does the work' (167k, 1.1k bookmarks), echoed by Marc Lou's 'end of UI for SaaS' (139k) and Amjad Masad's 'software is learning to run it'. Hassan's Bygga, a free open-source IKEA assembly guide with 3D and voice, was the most-saved watchlist post (2.4k bookmarks). Claude Duet split opinion: Alex Finn calls it the best personal agent he's tried (85k), while Riley Brown churned back to Claude Code Projects. Pieter Levels showed the setup behind his posts, everything on VPS servers with Claude Code over SSH, and his agent's magnesium check got 121k. Big lab news was science claims (Greg Brockman's three discoveries 3.08M, Anthropic's drug-discovery partnerships 2.49M) and new models (Genie 4 heading to the API, Liquid's LFM3 at 1.61M). Pieter's top post (413k) was about Spanish train deaths, off-lane for drafting, along with his vacuum review, stock and food posts. The meta: outcome-based pricing and 'one agent on your own data' setups are getting saved; treat lab science claims as claims until the papers are read.

drafts.angle: Give away the app, charge for the work
drafts.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg's line got 167k views and 1.1k bookmarks: give away the CRM, the dashboard and the app, and charge for the agent that does the work.

Marc Lou called it 'the end of UI for SaaS' the next morning (139k). Amjad Masad: 'Software ate the world, now it's learning to run it.'

If you sell software, write down the one outcome customers pay for. That outcome, done by an agent, is what you'll be pricing next year.
drafts.inspired_by: @gregisenberg saas is becoming free (167k) + @marclou end of UI for SaaS (139k) + @amasad software learning to run it (134k)
drafts.video_tip: 10s: a pricing page morphing from per-seat to per-task, caption price the outcome.

drafts.angle: One box, one agent, all your data
drafts.draft_en:
Pieter Levels runs everything from VPS servers: Termius for SSH, Claude Code on the box, and his businesses, calories and sleep data all pulled in. The same setup told him he was short on magnesium (121k views).

Theo shared a similar setup: he controls his machines from his phone over the internet, not through computer use.

The pattern isn't a new app. It's putting your data where one agent can read it.
drafts.inspired_by: @levelsio everything runs on my VPS (31k, 216 bookmarks) + @levelsio clanker magnesium check (121k) + @theo control machines from phone (25k)
drafts.video_tip: 12s: three data sources syncing into one server icon, then a phone asking it a question, caption one box.

drafts.angle: Agent that suggests vs agent you steer
drafts.draft_en:
Two takes on Claude Duet in one day.

Alex Finn: the most intelligent, proactive and friendly personal agent he's tried (85k views).
Riley Brown: churned, back on Claude Code Projects, where he picks the model and can run sessions on his own computer (67k).

Both are right for different people. Do you want ideas handed to you, or control? Answer that before you pick a tool.

scout_meta.method_note: Data came from the X API read connector (Grok Bot public read access): get_users_posts with exclude=replies,retweets from 2026-10-27 16:15 UTC, self-thread replies dropped, long texts from note_tweet. View counts are impression_count at ~11:20 CT Oct 28. Outsiders from account-group searches (AI labs, AI builders) and a keyword search (Claude Duet / Genie 4 / GPT-6.1 / AI agents / Claude Code) plus posts quoted by watchlist hits, all inside the last ~48h; off-topic and politics posts dropped. t3dotgg is stale (Theo posts as @theo, counted as outsider). Off-lane watchlist posts are kept as hits but flagged skip in drafts.
